title: Infraction-Resistant Policy Compiler and Contextual Enforcer
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Purpose: Build a policy compiler that translates high-level RBAC v2 rules into an efficient, explainable bytecode used by the runtime enforcer. The enforcer will run as middleware across API gateway, runtime serving layer, and Console admin endpoints and must provide contextual allow/deny decisions, reason strings for audit, and deterministic fallbacks when identity or attribute data is missing.

Scope:
- Declarative policy language subset and compiler
- Runtime enforcer middleware for API, serving runtime, and Console
- Audit enrichment pipeline to include decision_reason, matched_rules, identity_source
- SSO/SAML attribute mapping and SCIM-backed group sync integrations for identity resolution
- Fallback policies: neutral, deny-by-default toggle, and degraded-mode allow for read-only telemetry

Acceptance Criteria:
- Compiler produces policy bytecode with <=3ms average compile-time for policy sets up to 5k rules
- Enforcer latency tail P99 add <=2ms at target RPS after warm cache
- Decisions include decision_reason and rule_ids in audit logs
- End-to-end tests covering missing-attribute flows, cross-tenant isolation, and privileged role escalation
- Security review completed and signed off before canary rollout

Non-goals:
- Full policy authoring UI (only stable API + CLI)
- RBAC inference engine (out of scope for this ticket)

implementation_plan: Phase 1 — Compiler core and unit tests (2 wks)
Phase 2 — Runtime middleware adapters (API gateway, serving runtime, Console) + integration tests (3 wks)
Phase 3 — Audit enrichment pipeline and observability dashboards (1 wk)
Phase 4 — Security review, canary rollout to dedicated staging, roll-forward policy (1 wk)
risks: SCIM sync lag causing false-deny — mitigation: attribute freshness windows and fallback_mode=neutral option
Performance regression at high RPS — mitigation: caching compiled bytecode and hot-rule hotpath optimization
Policy complexity explosion — mitigation: limit on number of conjuncts per rule and compiler static analysis to warn on expensive predicates
testing: Unit tests for compiler IR and bytecode emitter
Integration tests for middleware across API/runtime/console
Chaos tests simulating identity-provider outages and SCIM inconsistencies
Audit log ingestion tests and schema validation
rollout: Canary on internal staging with 10% traffic for 72h
Gradual rollout to Dedicated tenants with opt-out window
